steps.content: The raging storm outside pelts the shelter walls with sand and stones, making the whole building groan ominously.
You huddle in a corner of the room, holding your comms device as close to your mouth as possible to ensure that your voice gets through clearly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Stay away from the center of the storm, and don't attempt any rescue operations... Yes, I'm safe for now. I'll contact you again once the storm passes.
You hear voices of the task force from the other end, broken and filled with static.

steps.speaker: Task Force
steps.content: Chief, thank good(static)... relieved you're safe. We found shelter(static)... we met some(static)... they showed us the way...

The wind on the other end grows louder until, after a few seconds of static, the calls cuts out completely. The Mania in the storm is interfering with the signals, leaving you totally cut off from the outside world.
Of course, I wouldn't mind if you called me "darling" instead—after all, we'll be wedded soon enough. You could also call me dear, honey, sweetheart... whatever you prefer, really.
A hand gently pats you on the back.
When you look up, the bounty hunter is nowhere to be seen.
[End of Flashback]

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sigh...

You set down the comms device and turn to survey the room. It's a mid-sized trading post near a transport route, used for handling accounts and temporary storage. Given the harsh environment of WhiteSands and the threat of desert bandits, it's also equipped with plenty of defensive gear.
But the furnishings are completely wrecked, and sand is spiraling in through holes in the windows. This place has clearly been abandoned for some time.
You approach a table in the room. There's a broken coffee cup on it with dried coffee stains inside—looks like someone had only drunk half of it before it dried out.

Stacks of messy accounting papers litter the desk. On one document, the calculation stops at a particular decimal point—the next number is distorted, with the pen stroke stretching into an unnatural line across the page.
...They left all these things behind. They must have left in a hurry.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Some kind of emergency... but there's no sign of looting or destruction. This doesn't look like desert bandits or an armed assault...

options: Could it have been a sandstorm?

choices.text: Could it have been a sandstorm?

steps.content: Bingo! You got it right.
A familiar teasing voice rings out beside you—Korryn had returned. She had put away her rifle, and is now holding a worn blanket, emergency rations, and a toolbox.

options: I thought you'd slipped away again.

choices.text: I thought you'd slipped away again.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: I went to gather some supplies. People take refuge here sometimes. It's a WhiteSands rule—you can take what you need from shelters, but you've got to leave something for the next person who comes along.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: I mean, I'd love to leave... But all those stories about adventuring through sandstorms are just fairy tales for kids. Even I'm not crazy enough to go into a storm alone.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Here, wrap yourself in this blanket. There's no telling how long this storm will last, and it gets freezing cold when the temperature drops.

options: You seem familiar with this place.

choices.text: You seem familiar with this place.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What exactly is this place? What happened to it?
She gives you the blanket and a bottle of water, then walks toward the drafty windows with her toolbox.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: As you can see, this used to be a trading hub before a massive Tide of Ashes turned the whole place upside down.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: The old, poorly maintained defenses couldn't hold up against the storm. Lucky for them, they had two sand boats and some Hypercube reserves, so most of the workers here managed to escape.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: But I heard they later got into legal trouble for misappropriating Hypercubes. Don't know how that turned out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A massive Tide of Ashes? When did this happen?

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Let me think... It happened sometime this year, right around the time of that big incident in DisCity...
As she hammers a long plank over the window frame, Korryn turns to you with a gleam in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: —I think it was the <color=#fb9259>Black Ring</color> incident in the Syndicate. What a coincidence, Chief. Any idea how these might be connected?

Dead silence fills the room. Korryn stands in the darkness, her face shadowed by the brim of her hat. You can't make out her expression, but you feel her gaze studying you, as if trying to unearth some hidden secret.
But more chilling than her demeanor are the connections she's suggesting—BR-002 and the Tide of Ashes? Could the escalating disturbances in WhiteSands be linked to the Black Ring?
And... could this be why Korryn kidnapped Hella? Was getting close to you her real objective all along?
Before you can respond, Korryn lets out a sigh.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Well, judging by that blank look on your face, I guess you don't know either.
She turns and walks back, as if suddenly remembering something. She feels around her pocket before tossing something your way.
You catch it reflexively. It lands heavily in your palm, and you look down to examine it.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Just a little bribe. Don't worry, it's clean. It's expired—but only by about ten days, so no big deal.
Korryn takes out an identical piece of candy, unwraps it and pops it into her mouth. She then walks over to sit beside you.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Come on, lighten up. I've got nothing against you. I just wanted to run something by someone from DisCity's upper brass to see if my hunch had any merit at all.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Too bad I picked the wrong person. Turns out you don't know anything either.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: I'll own up to it. I'm sorry for dragging you into this storm with me.
Her apology comes without pretense, and unlike her usual playful banter, her tone carries genuine sincerity.
The lizard Sheriff crawls leisurely around her neck and across her shoulder. It meets your gaze and blinks, as if offering its own apology.

options: This apology comes a bit late.

choices.text: This apology comes a bit late.

steps.content: But more than her apology, you're interested in something else she mentioned.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Besides this theory of yours, what else do you know?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The intensifying sandstorms and Tide of Ashes, the abandoned trade routes... These are things I can't see from DisCity. WhiteSands might face new threats in the future, but I'm blind to them. You're the one who knows what's really happening out here.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Korryn, what's troubling you? What did you really see?
You finally see Korryn's carefully maintained composure beginning to crack.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You've sensed it too... something's at work behind the scenes, right?
After those words sink in, Korryn falls silent for a moment. When she speaks again, it's as if she's surrendering to the inevitable.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Oh you silver-tongued devil—I give you candy to help your throat, and you use it to interrogate me? How ungrateful.
The young bounty hunter sits up.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Recent events... have started to line up with strange things from the past.
A long time ago... back when sandstorms weren't as frequent, and before I became a Sinner, I'd occasionally take on bounty cases—such as revenge or missing person cases.
The jobs came in all shapes and sizes, and so did the clients. Everyone in WhiteSands was just trying to scrape by, so no one asked too many questions about who was paying.
...but one particular client was different... unsettling in a way I'd never seen before.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: I've delivered what you asked for. But... isn't the payment a bit too generous? Don't tell me I just delivered something that's gonna get the attention of the cops!

steps.speaker: Shadowy Figure in Black
steps.content: No need to worry, young one.

steps.speaker: Shadowy Figure in Black
steps.content: We harbor no ill intent, nor will we cause you any trouble... We merely wish to establish a friendship.
With the transaction complete, the figure in black extends their hand courteously, and I return the gesture. Their hand was cold and unnaturally stiff.

steps.speaker: Shadowy Figure in Black
steps.content: Trust me, one day you'll be grateful for the payment you received today...
[Black Screen] (Flashback filter)

steps.speaker: Shadowy Figure in Black
steps.content: Farewell, Miss Korryn. <color=#fb9259>A pleasure doing business with you</color>.
It was a strange client and a strange job, and the payment made no sense. As time passed, I pushed the memory to the back of my mind—until—

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Korryn?! Korryn, what are you— cough cough—get out of here!
The sandstorm came out of nowhere. WhiteSands had never seen such a massive, sudden storm before. Tuco needed time to move out, so I stayed behind to cover their retreat.
Good thing I was the only one who stayed behind—the moment the convoy left, the storm devoured everything in its path. Including me, the last one standing.

In the chaos, all my senses blurred into nothing—except for the searing heat in my hands. The burning sensation started at my fingertips, growing hotter and hotter until it became almost unbearable, and then—

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: And then, when I finally woke up, I was wrapped up like a mummy on a Tuco vessel.
Korryn stares at her fingertips, lost in thought.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: It wasn't until later that I realized that burning sensation was Mania. I'd been infected by the Mania in the Tide of Ashes, becoming what you call a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: ...I still don't know who that person was, but they must have been planning something. My survival in that sandstorm was no coincidence.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: The world is changing rapidly. WhiteSands is getting more chaotic by the day—Hypercube prices are soaring, Nirvana is monopolizing the trade routes, and sandstorms are spinning out of control. Our chances of survival are slim enough as it is, and if there's more trouble brewing...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With your abilities, fleeing the crisis to DisCity shouldn't be too difficult.
Korryn laughs softly, but her words are heavy.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: But it won't be easy for Tuco, will it?

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: You know Tuco. The town has almost no able-bodied adults—mostly elderly, children, and people too weak or sick to fight. In other words, people DisCity won't take in.
As if recalling all those familiar faces, warmth seeps into Korryn's voice.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: We've survived on lies and tricks so far, but how much longer can we keep it up? No one knows. No one can make any promises.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: And there are so many places like Tuco scattered across WhiteSands... They might vanish beneath the sand without even knowing what hit them. No one hears their voices. No one even remembers they existed.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: So I decided to take the initiative and bait out someone from DisCity who looked like they might know something—
She flashes you a knowing look.

options: So I'm the unlucky chump from DisCity?

choices.text: So I'm the unlucky chump from DisCity?

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Bingo, dear!

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: I have to thank little Hella. At first I thought she was just bragging, but turns out she really does have deep ties with the MBCC. She's such a sweet girl, and the dummy Chief she trusted and adored must be a softie too—

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you set your trap, using Hella's kidnapping as bait to lure me to WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Yeah, but who knew our dear Chief would be such a handful and actually jump ship to chase after me? If anything had happened to you, that little mouse would've made me pay...

steps.speaker: Korryn
steps.content: Yes?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Aren't you the same? Love makes fools of us all. You snuck out of Tuco, thinking you could handle everything by yourself... We're not so different, you and I.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Rushing into danger alone without explaining anything... I've done that before too, but it only torments those you leave behind. It's not the right way.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your heart's in the right place, but...
...you've forgotten that it's precisely because the path ahead is so dark and uncertain that we need to face it together with our companions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can share some information with you, but I'm sure your companions wouldn't want to be kept in the dark either.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No one should die in WhiteSands, or be buried by these merciless sandstorms. At the very least, you all deserve to know what you're up against.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for playing hero and acting tough—
You can't help but tease the bounty hunter before you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Better save that for Hella—she's more of a sucker for that kind of thing.
Korryn freezes for a moment, about to protest, when a sudden noise interrupts her.
Bang bang! Thunderous strikes echo from the main door. For the first time, genuine shock crosses Korryn's face, like she's seen something that shouldn't be here...
The next second, the metal lock shatters with a spray of shrapnel. The door bursts open, slamming against the wall. Dark figures charge in yelling, lunging toward you like a storm.
Korryn you *******! I'm gonna rip your head off!!!
